conviction_note: The revenue number will very likely beat the company's own $5.3M guide (they beat the last three guides by 12-14%, and Barco said the Americas cinema market picked up in calendar Q2), but this stock has not paid for guide beats: release-day moves after those three beats were -0.3%, -1.9% and +4.3%. The one large recent move was -25.4% on last year's Q4 print, driven by the next-quarter guide, and that guide is the unknown this year too, so the two small findings offset and the honest net is about zero.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 revenue is likely to beat the $5.3M guide by roughly 10%. The company beat its last three quarterly guides by 12-14% (Q1 $5.58M vs $4.9M, Q2 $3.8M vs $3.4M, Q3 $3.39M vs ~$3.0M). Barco's 1H26 release (2026-07-15, after MITQ gave this guide) reported a cinema pick-up in the Americas in calendar Q2, which is MITQ's fiscal Q4, and June 2026 domestic box office was the highest since 2019.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Release-day close-to-close moves after the last three guide beats of 12-14% were -0.3% (2025-11-14), -1.9% (2026-02-12) and +4.3% (2026-05-14), from Yahoo daily bars. The baseline's history is keyed to 8-K filing dates, which trail the releases by 1-5 days, so it records other days (-8.38, +0.45, -1.13).
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is priced. A company that beats its guide 3 for 3 has taught holders to expect a beat, and the damped reactions show it: if the market had not expected a beat, the last three beats would have moved the stock clearly up. The only part that may not be priced is the size of the Q2 cinema pick-up that Barco reported after MITQ last spoke. That is sized small because the reaction function has not paid for this line.
findings.independence: Barco 1H26 results, 2026-07-15 (snippet only; the PDF could not be text-extracted): https://assets.barco.com/asset/500eac06-9067-4404-81a7-66803b4d79ab/2026-07-15-PR-1H26-Results-EN-1.pdf. Gower Street on record June 2026 box office: https://gower.st/articles/keeping-momentum-2026-sees-highest-grossing-june-quarter-first-half-this-decade-international-domestic-box-office/. findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 guide will be compared with a tough Q1 FY26 of $5.58M, which management said was inflated by 'accelerated delivery of projects previously expected later in the year'. With this company's conservative guiding, a guide below the prior year looks more likely than not. Last year's Q4 print, which came with a Q1 guide below the prior year's actual, fell -25.4% on release day (2025-09-25 close 1.26 to 2025-09-26 close 0.94).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-09-26 Q4 FY25 release (revenue -7.3% YoY, Q1 guide $4.9M vs prior-year Q1 $5.25M): -25.4% on 677,600 shares. The baseline misses this day and records +4.36% on 2025-09-29 instead. 2024-09-27 Q4 FY24 release: +1.4%. Yahoo chart: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/MITQ?period1=1758672000&period2=1759276800&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing in the filings has flagged the comparison; the name has no analysts and no preview. If the market were braced for a weak Q1 guide, the stock would have sold off into the print; instead it is +6% over 20 days. But the guide level itself is inference, not a document, so it is sized well below the name's large-move tail.
findings.independence: The company's own FY25 outlook said revenue was 'more weighted to the second half, given industry planning and budget cycles' (8-K ex99, 2025-09-29): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770236/000143774925030005/ex_833542.htm. It is the same company's guiding pattern, not an independent series.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR (data.sec.gov submissions): no NT 10-K, no 8-K item 4.01 (auditor change), no 4.02 (non-reliance), no 3.01 (listing deficiency) through 2026-09-23. They clean up compliance around the 10-K, involve no buying or selling, and change no line in the numbers. No source says what the review was about. The Q3 10-Q discloses material weaknesses (closing process, segregation of duties), but a write-down is unsourced speculation.
Unexplained volume of 995,700 shares with a +6.7% close on 2026-09-14; no news, no filing. Worth 0 under rule 5.
Company news from June to September 2026: none apart from the two call-scheduling releases (stocktitan news list). No new contract, installation or DCS order was disclosed after the Q3 call.
Q3 call transcript: no analyst questions, no FY27 guidance, no tariff commentary.
Short interest: 0.90% of float (finviz), not a squeeze setup.

baseline_tension: No options market means there is no skew to agree or disagree with. The run-up is +6.3% over 20 days and -5.9% over 5 days, and the delay produced no sustained sell-off. My two small findings roughly cancel, which agrees with a baseline that has no directional statement. The baseline's reaction history is keyed to 8-K filing dates that trail the releases, so it understates the tail: the real release-day moves include -25.4%.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): the beat finding was cut from +0.7 to +0.5. The name has not paid for guide beats (-0.3, -1.9, +4.3 on true release days), and the Barco / box-office support is an industry proxy (rule 5), not a company number.

Documents beat inference: the Q1-guide finding was cut from -1.5 to -0.6. The -25.4% reaction last year is a documented fact, but this year's guide level is a hypothesis with no primary document behind it, and the pessimism-artefact note applies.

Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number) and rule 5 (absence is not a cause): the delay / late-Section-16 / material-weakness finding (-0.7) was dropped. My own text said the back-filed Form 4s were equally consistent with routine 10-K compliance cleanup, and nothing sources a write-down.
Rule 7: short interest checked before any negative (0.90%, 0.74 days, finviz); not crowded, so the negative is not shrunk further for squeeze risk.

Final note on the reaction history: the baseline's history is keyed to 8-K filing dates that lag the releases. I rebuilt it from real release days, which reveals a -25.4% tail on Q4 prints, so the ranges were widened even though the point sizes shrank.
